sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of a line, the idiom 'turned their ___ on Him'. Nothing earlier lets them reason it out. The wrong answers (swords, bows) are weapons, while the right answer (backs) is a body part, so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The card opens by repeating the ox and donkey line from card 5 ('Even the DONKEY knows its master's manger'), which was already told. It moves nothing forward and works as a recap.
The answers are not the same kind of thing. 'Foreigners' are people, while 'locusts' and 'lions' are animals. This makes the right answer stand out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.
